Championship|2003 Greece]]|[[Australia national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} | FIBA_HOF_player = andrew-bogut }} '''Andrew Michael Bogut''' (born 28 November 1984) is an Australian professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is an assistant coach with the [[Sydney Kings]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). Bogut spent the majority of his career in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). The {{convert|7|ft|cm|0|adj=on}} tall [[Center (basketball)|center]] was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the [[NBA first overall draft pick|first overall pick]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]]. He earned [[All-NBA Third Team]] honors with the Bucks in 2010. Bogut was traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in 2012 and was named [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] in 2015, when he won an [[NBA championship]] with the Warriors. Bogut played [[college basketball]] for two years with the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]], and earned [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|national player of the year]] honors in 2005. He declared for the NBA draft, and became the first Australian to be the NBA's first overall pick. In his first year with the Bucks, Bogut was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] in 2006. He earned all-league honors in 2010 after averaging a career-high 15.9 points along with 10.2 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game. Bogut missed most of 2011–12 with an ankle injury, when he was traded to Golden State. After the Warriors won the NBA Finals in 2015, Bogut helped the Warriors win an NBA-record 73 games in 2015–16 and made his second Finals. Bogut was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]], where he played briefly before other short stints with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. In 2018, Bogut returned to his home country to play for the [[Sydney Kings]] and won the [[NBL Most Valuable Player Award]]. Following the [[2018–19 NBL season]], he signed back with the Warriors and made his third Finals in [[2019 NBA Finals|2019]]. Bogut then returned to the Kings for a second season before retiring in 2020. Described as one of the leading faces of Australian basketball, Bogut has been credited for serving as a cornerstone of the Australian national team, for paving the way for an entire generation of Australian players in the NBA and in playing a leading role in re-vitalizing the Australian NBL.{{cite web |last1=Kidane |first1=Benyam |title=The legacy of Andrew Bogut |date=2021-11-28 |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/nba/news/andrew-bogut-career-golden-state-warriors-australian-boomers-milwaukee-bucks/iaesglmfur3t1rlfugsr1bp4j |website=Sporting News |access-date=2020-05-25 }} ==Early life== Bogut was born in [[Melbourne]] on 28 November 1984.{{cite web |title=Andrew Bogut |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/44386/sid/8054/tid/239/tid2//_/2015_FIBA_Oceania_Championship/index.html |website=fiba.com |access-date=1 December 2025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151114222251/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/44386/sid/8054/tid/239/tid2//_/2015_FIBA_Oceania_Championship/index.html |archive-date=14 November 2015}} His parents, Michael and Anne, immigrated to Australia from [[Croatia]] in the 1970s,{{cite web |last=Brown |first=Daniel |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/ci_20234195/andrew-bogut-seven-things-about-warriors-new-7 |title=Andrew Bogut: Seven things about the Warriors' new 7-footer |work=MercuryNews.com |date=22 March 2012 |access-date=4 February 2016}} with his father from [[Osijek]] and his mother from [[Karlovac]].{{cite web |url=https://www.croatiaweek.com/nba-champ-andrew-bogut-i-grew-up-in-australia-but-was-raised-croatian/ |title=NBA champ Andrew Bogut: 'I grew up in Australia but was raised Croatian' |website=croatiaweek.com|date=February 21, 2023 |quote=Andrew was born in Melbourne in 1984 to parents who had migrated to Australia from Croatia in the 1970s. 'My mother is from Karlovac, and my dad is from Osijek,' Bogut says, before adding.}} Bogut grew up playing [[Australian rules football]] and tennis in addition to basketball. As a child, he patterned his basketball game after [[Toni Kukoč]], a Croatian [[NBA]] player who spent the majority of the 1990s playing for the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|last=Reed |first=Truman |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/MB_070413.html |title=Bucks Back When ... Andrew Bogut, Part I |work=NBA.com |date=13 April 2007 |access-date=4 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070510162815/http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/MB_070413.html |archive-date=10 May 2007 }} As a 15-year-old, Bogut was cut from the Victoria junior state representative team. In response to this setback, he began to improve his game with the help of Siniša Marković,{{cite news |url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/news/andrew-bogut-a-down-to-earth-nba-superstar/story-e6frf7jo-1111116948886 |title=Andrew Bogut a down-to-earth NBA superstar |work=HeraldSun.com.au |first=Mike joining the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] (AIS) in 2002.{{cite news|title=Past Athletes|work=ausport.gov.au|url=http://www.ausport.gov.au/ais/sports/basketball/athletes/past_athletes |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140212073754/http://www.ausport.gov.au/ais/sports/basketball/athletes/past_athletes|archive-date=12 February 2014|url-status=dead}} He competed for the [[BA Centre of Excellence|AIS men's team]] in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]] (SEABL) in 2002 and 2003, helping the AIS win the [[List of SEABL champions|East Conference title]] in his first season and won the SEABL East MVP in his second season.{{cite web|url=http://www.ababasketball.net.au/fs_newsitem.asp?id=3075&orgID=101&Oname=ABA&O1c=11&O10c=11|title=SEABL MVP|work=ABABasketball.net.au|date=24 August 2003|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030926061323/http://www.ababasketball.net.au/fs_newsitem.asp?id=3075&orgID=101&Oname=ABA&O1c=11&O10c=11|archive-date=26 September 2003|access-date=26 July 2024}} Bogut later joined the U-19 Australian junior national team, and was named the [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup MVP|most valuable player]] of the [[2003 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2003 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]], in Greece, after leading the Emus to the title. In eight games, he averaged 26.3 points, 17 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.5 blocks per game, and he shot 61 percent from the field and 74 percent from the free throw line. One of the highlights of his MVP conquest was a 22-point, 18-rebound performance, in a 106–85 victory over the US, in the quarterfinals of the medal round.{{cite web|last=Reed |first=Truman |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/MB_070416.html |title=Bucks Back When ... Andrew Bogut, Part II |work=NBA.com |date=16 April 2007 |access-date=4 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080724193940/http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/MB_070416.html |archive-date=24 July 2008 }} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]] in 2003–04, Bogut averaged 12.5 points and 9.9 rebounds in 33 games. He subsequently earned CollegeInsider.com All-Freshman Team honours, Mountain West Conference Freshman of the Year, second-team All-Mountain West Conference, and NABC second-team All-District 13.{{cite web|url=http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/andrew_bogut_73116.html |title=Andrew Bogut Bio |work=UtahUtes.com |access-date=4 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322150444/http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/andrew_bogut_73116.html |archive-date=22 March 2016 }} As a sophomore in 2004–05, Bogut started all 35 games for the Utes, leading them to a 29–6 record, the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Tournament, and a Mountain West Conference championship. He led the nation with 26 double-doubles and scored in double figures in 37 consecutive games dating back to the final two games of the 2003–04 season to have the sixth-longest streak in the country. He ranked 19th in the NCAA in scoring (20.4 ppg), second in rebounding (12.2 rpg) and eighth in field goal percentage (62.0), and led the Mountain West Conference in scoring, rebounding and field goal percentage. He became one of 31 Utah players all-time to score 1,000 points in his career, but just the third to reach that mark in two seasons. He was named the 2004–05 national player of the year by both ESPN.com and Basketball Times, and earned Associated Press first-team All-American and leading vote getter, becoming the 11th Ute all-time to earn All-America honours. Bogut also earned [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] honours and the [[John R. Wooden Award]].{{cite web|title=Andrew Bogut |work=woodenaward.com |url=http://www.woodenaward.com/andrew_bogut |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024051844/http://www.woodenaward.com/andrew_bogut |archive-date=24 October 2015 |url-status=live |df=dmy }} He later had his No. 4 jersey retired by Utah. ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2005–2012)=== [[File:AndrewBogutrebound.jpg|thumb|Bogut in 2005|left]] Bogut was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the first overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]], becoming the first Australian player and the second Utah player (the first being [[Bill McGill]]) to be drafted number one overall. As a rookie in 2005–06, he earned All-Rookie First Team honours and finished third in votes for the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]]. He played in all 82 regular season games for the Bucks in his first season, averaging 9.4 points and 7.0 rebounds per game. Bogut's second season in the league was cut short after he sprained his left foot and was put on the injured reserve for the final 15 games. He had previously played in 153 consecutive games.{{cite news |url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/breaking-news/bogut-out-for-the-season/story-e6frf33c-1111113204396 |title=Bogut out for the season |work=FoxSports.com |first=James |last=Dampney |date=22 March 2007 |access-date=4 February 2016}} He improved his numbers in 2006–07 to 12.3 points and 8.8 rebounds per game. In the [[2007–08 NBA season]], Bogut set career-highs in points (14.3), rebounds (9.8), blocks (1.7), steals (0.8) and minutes (34.9) per game.{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bogutan01.html |title=Andrew Bogut NBA Stats |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=4 February 2016}} He tallied a career-high 29 points against the Phoenix Suns in December and finished 9th in the NBA in blocks, 11th in rebounding and 12th in double-doubles (38). He started in 78 games for the Bucks, missing just four games through injury.{{cite news |url=http://www.basketball.net.au/bogut-soars-in-200708-nba-full-season-recap/ |title=BOGUT SOARS IN 2007/08 NBA FULL SEASON RECAP |work=Basketball.net.au |date=18 April 2008 |access-date=4 February 2016}} In the 2008 offseason, Bogut signed a five-year, $60 million extension that would keep him under contract through the 2013–14 season. The deal also had $12.5 million in possible incentives.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3480697|title=Agent says Bucks' Bogut will sign 5-year, $60M extension|date=July 9, 2008 |access-date=June 6, 2025}} Bogut appeared in just 36 games for the Bucks in 2008–09, missing the final 31 games of the season with a stress fracture in his lower back.{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2009-11-21/bogut-concerned-about-injury-run/1151128 |title=Bogut concerned about injury run |work=ABC.net.au |date=21 November 2009 |access-date=4 February 2016}} He faced more time on the sidelines during the 2009–10 season due to a strained ligament and bruise in his left leg. On 3 April 2010, near the end of a breakout season, Bogut suffered a major injury. That night, in a game against the [[Phoenix Suns]] at the [[Bradley Center]], Bogut had a chance to score on a fast break attempt. As he went up, [[Amar'e Stoudemire]] appeared to make some contact with Bogut and he lost his balance while completing the dunk. He hung onto the rim for a brief moment to try to right himself but could not, and fell at an awkward angle. Placing his right arm out to break the fall, Bogut landed with all of his weight on top of his wrist and his arm twisted as he landed.{{cite web |first=Charles F. |last=Gardner |url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/bucks/89851432.html |title=Bucks 107, Suns 98; Bucks lose Bogut for the season |work=jsonline.com |date=4 April 2010 |access-date=4 February 2016}} The next day, Bogut was diagnosed with a broken hand, dislocated elbow and sprained wrist, injuries that kept him out of for the remainder of the 2009–10 season.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5053689 |title=Bucks' Bogut out indefinitely |work=ESPN.com |date=4 April 2010 |access-date=4 February 2016}} In what was a breakout season for Bogut, he finished with averages of 15.9 points, 10.2 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game, earning All-NBA Third Team honours, becoming first Bucks player named to the squad since [[Michael Redd]] in 2003–04.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bogut_allnba_100506.html |title=Bogut named to All-NBA Third Team |work=NBA.com |date=6 May 2010 |access-date=4 February 2016}} Bogut helped the Bucks to a 46–36 record, their most wins since going 50–32 in 2000–01, and their first playoff appearance since 2006. Bogut returned to the Bucks' line-up in 2010–11, playing in 65 games and leading the league in blocks with 2.6 per game.{{cite web |url=http://www.basketball.net.au/andrew-bogut-journey-nba-championship-ring/ |title=ANDREW BOGUT – A JOURNEY TO AN NBA CHAMPIONSHIP RING |work=Basketball.net.au |date=17 June 2015 |access-date=4 February 2016}} [[File:Andrew Bogut pass.jpg|thumb|Bogut in 2011]] During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Bogut chose to return home to Australia and play in the NBL for the [[2011–12 NBL season|2011–12 season]]. He was linked to the [[Gold Coast Blaze]], [[Adelaide 36ers]] and the team he supported when growing up, the [[Sydney Kings]]. Ultimately, he chose the Kings (who finished last in [[2010–11 NBL season|2010–11]]), but the insurance to cover his remaining $39m contract with the Bucks could not be resolved, leaving the Kings and the NBL without his on-court services.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7066742/andrew-bogut-milwaukee-bucks-deal-australian-team-agent-says |title=Andrew Bogut won't play in Australia |work=ESPN.com |first=Marc |last=Stein |date=6 October 2011 |access-date=4 February 2016}} Following the breakdown in contract negotiations over the insurance money, Bogut stated he would like to join the Kings coaching staff in a bid not only to help the club, but help raise the NBL's profile. This, however, did not occur and he later returned to the Bucks following the conclusion of the lockout. On 25 January 2012, he fractured his ankle, ruling him out for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Andrew Bogut out indefinitely |date=29 November 2012 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8689937/andrew-bogut-golden-state-warriors-admits-microfracture-surgery-indefinitely |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121202021040/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/8689937/andrew-bogut-golden-state-warriors-admits-microfracture-surgery-indefinitely |archive-date=2 December 2012 |url-status=live |df=dmy }} ===Golden State Warriors (2012–2016)=== [[File:Andrew Bogut and David Lee.jpg|thumb|left|Bogut (left) with [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]] in 2013]] On 13 March 2012, Bogut and [[Stephen Jackson]] were traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for [[Monta Ellis]], [[Ekpe Udoh]] and [[Kwame Brown]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_acquire_bogut_jackson.html | title=Warriors Acquire Andrew Bogut and Stephen Jackson From Milwaukee | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=13 March 2012 | access-date=14 March 2012}} According to the Warriors, he underwent surgery in April to "clean out loose particles and bone spurs in the ankle". Bogut sat out the [[2012–13 Golden State Warriors season|2012–13]] preseason, but played in four of the first five regular season games, averaging just 6.0 points and 3.8 rebounds. He was then declared out indefinitely. Bogut received [[Regenokine]] treatment to aid his recovery in late November,{{cite news|last=Amick |first=Sam |title=Bogut is getting blood manipulation treatments |date=15 November 2012 |work=hoopsworld.com |url=http://www.hoopsworld.com/andrew-bogut-is-getting-blood-manipulation-treatments/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121126082430/http://www.hoopsworld.com/andrew-bogut-is-getting-blood-manipulation-treatments/ |archive-date=26 November 2012 |url-status=live |df=dmy }} and it was also revealed that his procedure in April was more serious [[microfracture surgery]] than previously thought. Bogut returned on 28 January 2013, recording 12 points, eight rebounds, two assists, and four blocks in a road victory over the [[Toronto Raptors]]. On 2 May, during Game 6 of the first round of the playoffs, Bogut recorded playoff career-highs of 14 points and 21 rebounds. He also became the first Warriors player with 20 playoff rebounds since [[Larry Smith (basketball, born 1958)|Larry Smith]] had 23 on 12 May 1987 against the Los Angeles Lakers. On 25 October 2013, Bogut signed a three-year, $36 million contract extension with the Warriors.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14646 |title=Warriors sign Andrew Bogut to contract extension |access-date=26 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150417070357/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14646 |archive-date=17 April 2015 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }} Despite another injury-riddled season in 2013–14, he still finished 10th in NBA Defensive Player of the Year voting and became the first player in franchise history to average at least 10 rebounds per game while shooting 60 percent from the field.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/blogs/dotcom/1314recap_bogut |title=2013–14 Season Review: Andrew Bogut |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=8 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150218071437/http://www.nba.com/warriors/blogs/dotcom/1314recap_bogut |archive-date=18 February 2015 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }} After playing well through the first 19 games of the 2014–15 season, Bogut injured his right knee on 8 December 2014 against the Minnesota Timberwolves and subsequently missed 12 games. He returned to action off the bench against Indiana on 7 January 2015, recording four points and eight rebounds in a 117–102 victory.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150107/INDGSW/gameinfo.html |title=Thompson scores 40, Warriors beat Pacers 117-102 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=8 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150504153036/http://www.nba.com/games/20150107/INDGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-date=4 May 2015 |url-status=dead }} On 2 March, Bogut scored a season-high 16 points in a loss to the Brooklyn Nets.[http://www.nba.com/games/20150302/GSWBKN/gameinfo.html Jack's jumper gives Nets 110-108 win over Curry, Warriors] On 7 April, he had eight points and a career-high nine blocks in a loss to the New Orleans Pelicans.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150407/GSWNOP/gameinfo.html|title=Pelicans beat Warriors 103-100, move into 8th spot|work=NBA.com|date=7 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150410092129/http://www.nba.com/games/20150407/GSWNOP/gameinfo.html|archive-date=10 April 2015}} Bogut and the Warriors won the [[2015 NBA Finals]] after defeating the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in six games despite a 2–1 deficit. Disappointed in the way he ended the 2014–15 season, Bogut removed all processed sugars from his diet during the 2015 off-season and subsequently came into training camp in October 2015 with improved athleticism, having lost {{Convert|22|lb|kg}}.[http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/72749150/australian-nba-star-andrew-bogut-drops-10kg-in-offseason-after-cutting-sugar-from-his-diet Australian NBA star Andrew Bogut drops 10kg in off-season after cutting sugar from his diet] On 9 February 2016, Bogut had a season-best game with 13 points, 11 rebounds, three steals and a season-high six blocked shots in a 123–110 victory over the Houston Rockets.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160209/HOUGSW/gameinfo.html Curry leads Warriors past Rockets for 42nd straight home win] The Warriors broke the NBA record for most wins in a season with 73, eclipsing the 72 wins set by the [[1995–96 Chicago Bulls season|1995–96 Chicago Bulls]]. In Game 5 of the Western Conference Finals match-up with the Oklahoma City Thunder on 26 May, Bogut recorded a playoff career-high 15 points and 14 rebounds to help the Warriors send the series to a Game 6 with a 120–111 victory at home, cutting the Thunder's advantage in the series to 3–2.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160526/OKCGSW/gameinfo.html |title=Defending champion Warriors stave off elimination, beat OKC |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=27 May 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160528163630/http://www.nba.com/games/20160526/OKCGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-date=28 May 2016 |url-status=dead }} The Warriors went on to win the series in seven games and advanced to the [[2016 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] for the second straight year, where they would again face the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. On 15 June, he was ruled out for six to eight weeks after suffering a left knee injury during Game 5 of the NBA Finals two days prior.[http://www.nba.com/warriors/andrew-bogut-update-6.15.16 Andrew Bogut Update 6.15.16] The Warriors went on to lose the series in seven games despite a 3–1 lead. ===Dallas Mavericks (2016–2017)=== On 7 July 2016, Bogut was traded, along with a future second-round pick, to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for a top-55 protected 2019 second-round pick that eventually wasn't converted.{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-acquire-center-andrew-bogut-warriors/|title=Mavericks acquire center Andrew Bogut from Warriors|work=mavs.com|date=7 July 2016|access-date=7 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818220200/http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-acquire-center-andrew-bogut-warriors/|archive-date=18 August 2016|url-status=dead}} The trade was made by the Warriors to free up salary cap space for their signing of [[Kevin Durant]]. Bogut made his Mavericks debut in the season opener on 26 October 2016, recording six points, six rebounds, three assists, and a block in a 130–121 overtime loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400899379|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161027125118/http://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400899379|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 October 2016|title=Turner's opening act leads Pacers past Mavs, 130-121 in OT|work=NBA.com|date=26 October 2016|access-date=26 October 2016}} On 3 December, he had a game-high 11 rebounds and a season-high eight points in a 107–82 victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899738|title=Barnes, Matthews power Mavericks past Bulls 107-82|work=ESPN.com|date=3 December 2016|access-date=4 December 2016}} Bogut went on to miss 11 games in December with a right knee injury,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899916|title=Harden, Rockets top Mavs 123-107 in technical-marred game|work=ESPN.com|date=27 December 2016|access-date=27 December 2016}} and a further six games in January with a right hamstring strain.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900109|title=Barnes scores 23 to lead Mavericks over Knicks, 103-95|work=ESPN.com|date=25 January 2017|access-date=26 January 2017}} On 23 February 2017, Bogut was traded, along with [[Justin Anderson (basketball)|Justin Anderson]] and a protected first-round pick, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Nerlens Noel]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/nerlens-release-draft|title=Philadelphia 76ers Acquire First-Round Pick, Justin Anderson, and Andrew Bogut From Dallas|work=NBA.com|date=23 February 2017|access-date=23 February 2017}} Four days later, he was waived by the 76ers.{{cite web|last=Vardon|first=Joe|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2017/02/andrew_bogut_waived_by_76ers_c.html|title=Andrew Bogut waived by 76ers, Cavs hopeful to sign him|work=Cleveland.com|date=27 February 2017|access-date=27 February 2017}}{{cite web|last=Stein|first=Marc|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/18783679/los-angeles-lakers-waive-jose-calderon-philadelphia-76ers-waive-andrew-bogut|title=76ers waive Andrew Bogut, Lakers waive Jose Calderon to complete buyouts|work=ESPN.com|date=27 February 2017|access-date=27 February 2017}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2017)=== On 2 March 2017, Bogut signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/bogut-signing-170302|title=OFFICIAL: Cavs Sign Andrew Bogut|work=NBA.com|date=2 March 2017|access-date=2 March 2017}} Four days later, Bogut broke his left leg 56 seconds into his Cleveland debut. Initial X-rays revealed a fractured tibia, and he was subsequently taken to the [[Cleveland Clinic]] for further tests.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900331|title=Bogut breaks leg in debut, Cavs lose 106-98 to Heat|work=ESPN.com|date=6 March 2017|access-date=6 March 2017}} There, Bogut's tibia was set, and he was scheduled to undergo a non-surgical treatment and recovery plan. Bogut was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the regular season and playoffs.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/status-updates-170308|title=Status Update on Bogut, Korver, Smith and Coach Lue|work=NBA.com|date=8 March 2017|access-date=8 March 2017}} As a result, he was waived by the Cavaliers on 13 March.{{cite web|last=Withers|first=Tom|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/03/13/cavaliers-sign-larry-sanders-waive-andrew-bogut|title=Cleveland Cavaliers sign forward Larry Sanders, waive Andrew Bogut|work=NBA.com|date=13 March 2017|access-date=13 March 2017}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2017–2018)=== On 19 September 2017, Bogut signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170919-andrew-bogut-signs|title=Lakers Sign Andrew Bogut|work=NBA.com|date=19 September 2017|access-date=19 September 2017}} He made his Lakers debut in the season opener on 19 October, committing three fouls and three turnovers in a 108–92 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974442|title=Deflated Ball: Blake gets 29 in Clips' 108-92 rout of Lakers|work=ESPN.com|date=19 October 2017|access-date=20 October 2017}} On 6 January 2018, Bogut was waived by the Lakers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180106-bogut-waived|title=Lakers Waive Andrew Bogut|work=NBA.com|date=6 January 2018|access-date=6 January 2018}} He did not return to the NBA that season in order to remain in Australia with his pregnant wife.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/03/27/andrew-bogut-wont-return-nba-season-pregnant-wife|title=Andrew Bogut remains in Australia with pregnant wife, won't seek late-season NBA contract|work=NBA.com|date=27 March 2018|access-date=27 March 2018}} ===Sydney Kings (2018–2019)=== On 24 April 2018, Bogut signed a two-year deal with the [[Sydney Kings]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/41623-australian-legend-andrew-bogut-signs-with-sydney-kings|title=Australian Legend Andrew Bogut Signs with Sydney Kings|work=NBL.com.au|date=24 April NBL season|2018–19 regular season]], he was named the [[NBL Most Valuable Player Award|NBL Most Valuable Player]] after averaging 11.6 points per game to go with 329 rebounds, 98 assists, and 77 blocks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/nbl-awards-bogut-wins-andrew-gaze-trophy-as-mvp|title=NBL Awards: Bogut wins Andrew Gaze Trophy as MVP|work=NBL.com.au|date=17 February web|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/nbl/gracious-sydney-kings-star-andrew-bogut-says-perth-wildcat-bryce-cotton-shouldve-won-nbl-mvp-award-ng-b881108562z|title=Gracious Sydney Kings star Andrew Bogut says Perth Wildcat Bryce Cotton should've won NBL MVP award|work=TheWest.com.au|date=18 February 2019|access-date=18 February 2019}} Bogut was also named the [[NBL Best Defensive Player Award|Best Defensive Player]] and earned [[All-NBL Team|All-NBL First Team]] honours. He helped the Kings reach the playoffs with an 18–10 record and a third-place finish, before losing 2–0 to [[Melbourne United]] in the semi-finals.{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/casper-cg43s-53-lift-melbourne-into-grand-final|title=Casper and CG43's 53 lift Melbourne into Grand Final|work=NBL.com.au|date=3 March 2019|access-date=5 March 2019}} In 30 total games, Bogut averaged 11.4 points, a league-high 11.6 rebounds, 3.4 assists, and 2.7 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bogut-signing-20190306|title=Warriors Sign Center Andrew Bogut|work=NBA.com|date=6 March 2019|access-date=6 March 2019}} === Return to Golden State (2019) === On 6 March 2019, after the conclusion of the [[2018–19 NBL season]], Bogut signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the rest of the [[2018–19 NBA season]]. His deal with the Warriors was allowed by the Kings with the condition that he honoured the second year of his two-year contract.{{cite web|url=https://warriorswire.usatoday.com/2019/04/22/andrew-bogut-confirms-return-to-the-sydney-kings-in-2019-20/|title=Andrew Bogut confirms return to the Sydney Kings in 2019-20|work=USA Today|first=Aneesh|last=Namburi|date=22 April 2019|access-date=16 August 2019}} The Warriors reached the [[2019 NBA Finals]], where they lost in six games to the [[Toronto Raptors]]. === Return to Sydney (2019–2020) === Bogut rejoined the Sydney Kings for the [[2019–20 NBL season]] and helped them win the minor premiership with a first-place finish and a 20–8 record. He was named to the [[All-NBL Team|All-NBL Second Team]].{{cite news |last1=Gilhooly |first1=Daniel |title=NBL award winners announced |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/28714451/nbl-award-winners-announced |access-date=21 February 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=16 February 2020}} On 25 May 2020, Bogut announced that he would not be re-signing with the Kings.{{cite web |title=Andrew Bogut's future up in the air after making huge Kings announcement |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/andrew-bogut-pulls-plug-on-sydney-kings-deal-in-shock-announcement/news-story/20c7a0de844c4f78f7d84bad351db538 |website=Fox Sports Australia |date=25 May 2020 |access-date=25 May 2020}}{{cite web |title=Andrew Bogut opts out of Sydney Kings, but not retired yet |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/29217272/andrew-bogut-quits-nbl-team-sydney-kings-not-retired-yet |website=ESPN |date=25 May 2020 |access-date=25 May 2020}}{{cite web |title=Bogut to take break from basketball amid coronavirus uncertainty |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/bogut-to-take-break-from-basketball-amid-coronavirus-uncertainty-20200525-p54w51.html |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=25 May 2020 |publisher=Fairfax Media |access-date=25 May 2020}} Bogut had two surgeries in 2020, one to remove a bone spur in his ankle and the other to help with sciatica in his lower back.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/andrew-bogut-announces-retirement|title=Andrew Bogut Announces Retirement|work=NBL.com.au|date=1 December 2020|access-date=1 December 2020}} ===Retirement=== On 1 December 2020, Bogut announced his retirement from basketball, citing numerous injury issues as the main reason.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/nbl-congratulates-andrew-bogut|title=NBL Congratulates Andrew Bogut|work=NBL.com.au|date=1 December 2020|access-date=1 December 2020}} ==National team career== Bogut started for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Boomers]] at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Athens Olympics]], averaging 13.7 points, 9.0 rebounds and 1.2 blocked shots and shooting 58.0% from the field. He represented Australia again in the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]. Australia advanced to the Round of 16 before losing to the [[United States national basketball team|United States]]. Bogut averaged 12.8 points per game and 6.2 rebounds per game during the tournament, leading Australia in both categories. He started for the Boomers at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Beijing Olympics]]. In 2012, Bogut was unable to play for the Boomers in the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|London Olympics]], as he had previously broken his left ankle in January during the 2011–12 NBA season.{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2012-03-16/bogut27s-future-hinges-on-ankle-scans/3894590 |title=Bogut's Olympics future hinges on ankle scans |work=ABC.net.au |date=16 March 2012 |access-date=4 February 2016}} On 14 July 2015, Bogut was named in the Australian Boomers squad for their European tour and the [[2015 FIBA Oceania Championship]].[http://www.basketball.net.au/australian-boomers-team-named-2015-internationals/ AUSTRALIAN BOOMERS' TEAM NAMED FOR 2015 INTERNATIONALS] The following year, he was a member of the Boomers team that finished in fourth place at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Olympic Games]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]]. This equaled Australia's best ever finish at the [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympics]], with the Boomers having also finished fourth in [[Basketball at the 1988 Summer Olympics|1988]], [[Basketball at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|1996]] and [[Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2000]]. In 2019, the Boomers again finished fourth, this time at the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|FIBA Basketball World Cup]] in China. In May 2025, Bogut was inducted into the [[FIBA Hall of Fame]], becoming the ninth Australian to be honored.{{cite news |title=Bogut joins game's elite |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bogut-joins-games-elite |access-date=19 May 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=19 May 2025 |language=en}}{{cite news |title=Andrew Bogut inducted into FIBA Hall of Fame Class of 2025 |url=https://www.australia.basketball/news/4199425/andrew-bogut-inducted-into-fiba-hall-of-fame-class-of-2025 |access-date=19 January 2025 |work=www.australia.basketball |date=16 January 2025 |language=en}} ==Coaching career== On 12 March 2025, Bogut was appointed as an assistant coach of the [[Sydney Kings]] for the [[2025–26 NBL season]].{{cite news |title=Bogut joins Kings coaching staff |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bogut-joins-kings-coaching-staff |access-date=12 March 2025 |work=NBL Official Website |date=12 March 2025}} ==Political views== In November and December 2016, on [[Twitter]], Bogut made a series of tweets in which he implied he believed elements of the [[Pizzagate]] hoax were real.[https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ftw/2016/12/07/andrew-bogut-believed-the-pizzagate-fake-news-story-which-makes-us-really-sad/95086624/ Andrew Bogut pushed the Pizzagate conspiracy], ''[[USA TODAY]]'' Sports, Nina Mandell, 7 December 2016. Retrieved 28 August 2021. At the time, the hoax had rapidly evolved into an elaborate [[conspiracy theory]] that ostensibly involved child sex trafficking, [[Hillary Clinton]], political strategist [[John Podesta]] and other Democrats, and it was supposedly centred in the (actually nonexistent) basement of a [[Washington, D.C.]], [[pizza parlor]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2016/12/10/business/media/pizzagate.html |title=Dissecting the #PizzaGate Conspiracy Theories |last1=Huang |first1=Gregor |last2=Aisch |first2=Jon |date=10 December 2016 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=18 September 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161210112745/http://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2016/12/10/business/media/pizzagate.html |archive-date=10 December 2016 |last3=Kang |first3=Cecilia}} In 2021, via his [[Instagram]] account, Bogut posted multiple times about coronavirus lockdowns. The lockdown, Victoria's sixth, prompted Bogut to vent his frustration due to [[Foodbank]] Victoria being closed because of concerns it was a coronavirus hotspot. He also believed that the lockdowns were already disproportionately affecting the [[working class]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.skynews.com.au/opinion/andrew-bogut-we-need-to-find-middle-ground-in-learning-to-live-with-covid/video/9d5a7d594b31fbaa12b3010952cd95e4|title=Andrew Bogut: We need to find 'middle ground' in 'learning to live with COVID'|date=23 August 2021}}{{cite book | url=https://www.parliament.vic.gov.au/file_uploads/PAEC_59-08_Vic_Gov_response_to_COVID-19_pandemic_YKNbjt2Y.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210202021738/https://www.parliament.vic.gov.au/file_uploads/PAEC_59-08_Vic_Gov_response_to_COVID-19_pandemic_YKNbjt2Y.pdf | url-status=dead | archive-date=2 February 2021 | title=Inquiry into the Victorian Government's response to the COVID-19 pandemic | publisher=Parliament of Victoria | date=February 2021 | isbn=978-1-922425-19-5 | accessdate=15 November 2021 }}{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/andrew-bogut-slams-covid19-lockdowns-news-instagram-video-dan-andrew/news-story/f0ae418fc288dd09ec9c4771a73f0893|title = 'I'm enemy number one': Bogut claims athletes muzzled over Covid-19 views in wild rant|date = 22 August 2021}}[https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Andrew-Bogut-Australia-lockdown-COVID-conspiracy-16405360.php Former Warriors center Andrew Bogut goes on long rant against Australia's COVID-19 lockdowns], ''[[SF Gate]]'', Eric Ting, 23 August 2021. Retrieved 24 August 2021. Bogut also claimed in his post that he had been approached to promote public health measures for money but declined, further stating without significant evidence that many other unnamed Australian celebrities were supposedly being compensated for urging that the public adhere to [[pandemic]] control measures despite many celebrities not being subject to the same rules as the working class. Bogut then urged other celebrities to speak out for residents, proclaiming "The silence was deafening".{{Cite web|url=https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-australia-governments-slammed-hotel-quarantine-treatment-celebrities-residents-covid19/2757cc5e-f865-45fc-a614-1229337ec93f|title = Governments slammed for 'treating celebs different to residents' in quarantine| date=22 July 2020 }} In January 2022, Bogut claimed on his social media that the Victorian government was attempting to 'silence him' after receiving a letter from the [[Victorian Electoral Commission]] over social media posts he had posted supporting the passing of a bill aimed at diminishing the pandemic powers of the government. The electoral commission denied the claims, stating that the basis of the letter was over Bogut's failure to have his posts authorised.{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/basketball-star-andrew-bogut-accuses-victorian-government-of-wanting-to-silence-him/news-story/d119417183da190a7ad5e988bc78c6a3|title = Basketball star Andrew Bogut accuses Victorian government of wanting to 'silence' him|date = 20 January 2022}} On 15 December 2024, Bogut posted a photo on one of his social media accounts which shows him hugging controversial singer [[Marko Perković]] whose songs glorify Croatian [[nationalism]] and [[chauvinism]] and promote the [[World War II]]-era [[fascist]] [[Ustaše]] [[dictatorship]].{{cite web |url=https://www.index.hr/sport/clanak/bivsa-nba-zvijezda-objavila-fotografiju-s-thompsonom-kazu-da-sam-lud/2624913.aspx |title=Bivša NBA zvijezda objavila fotografiju s Thompsonom |website=Index.hr |date=16 December 2024}}{{in lang|hr}} ==Personal life== Bogut and his wife, Jessica, have two sons, Luka and Nikola.{{cite web |title=Andrew Bogut considering retirement but delayed Olympics
